status_note: The client calls a POI-5-only adaptation API (IOUtils.setByteArrayMaxOverride) in production while on POI 5.2.4, so the adaptation is causally POI-5-triggered. NOT yet differential-verified.
discovery_method: Phase 2 external mining: GitHub code search for the POI-5 adaptation signature 'setByteArrayMaxOverride', then find_adaptation.py-style history check.

behavioral_break.why_it_breaks: POI 5.0 introduced a default maximum byte-array size in IOUtils; reading data larger than the default throws at runtime, so extraction/parsing silently fails. Compiles fine against POI 5 -> behavioural. The fix raises the limit via IOUtils.setByteArrayMaxOverride(n), a POI-5-only API.

adaptation.author: Nguyen Thanh
adaptation.summary: Raised POI's byte-array limit to 200 MB to allow processing large documents under POI 5's stricter default cap.
adaptation.caveat: First appearance of the call in git history is a general commit ("remove unnecessary things"); small project. POI version at that commit confirmed as 5.2.4.

verification.differential_needed: Build the repo, apply the POI 4->5 bump to pre-adaptation code, confirm the byte-limit break manifests and that setByteArrayMaxOverride resolves it (or a generated mimic test).
verification.standalone_repro_note: A standalone mimic (IOUtils.toByteArray with a large declared length) was attempted 2026-07-01 and did NOT reproduce the break: POI's byte cap is enforced deep in its document/record parsing, not at the top-level API (toByteArray just allocates until OOM). A faithful repro needs a crafted document or the repo's own parsing path (repo build required). Unlike xstream's one-call ForbiddenClassException, this parser-internal break is not standalone-reproducible.
verification.conclusion: Signature-confirmed POI-5 production adaptation; full BBC verification pending (standalone mimic insufficient - see standalone_repro_note).
